description.narrative:
Effective Institutions Platform (EIP) is a network of more than 60 countries and organisations in support of evidence based political dialogue, knowledge sharing and "peer-to-peer" learning about public sector reform. EIP support its members in the development of accountable, inclusive and tranpsarent public administrations that can deliver effective services for sustainable development.
EIP was founded in 2012 as a response to international committments to improve the efficiency of public institutions, and has since then developed into a mechanism for innovation and collegial exchange between governments. OECD hosts the platform and acts as its secretariat, but unlike other P2P mechanisms under the OECD's purview the EIP has a broad membership, not just OECD coutnries. Members incude both donor and partner countries, development banks, civil society and UN Agencies.
The overall purpose of the EIP is to contribute to the achievement of the sustainable development goals, especially goal 16, and advancing the aid effectiveness agenda by acting as a global knowledge hub on peer-to-peer learning approaches and providing a platform to facilitate incubation and learning on alternative and innovative approaches to public sector reform and institutional development, going beyond P2P methods.

The Effective Institutions Platform (EIP) är ett nätverk med över 60 länder och organisationer som stöder evidensbaserad politisk dialog, kunskapsdelning och ”peer-to-peer” (P2P) lärande om offentlig förvaltning och institutionella reformer. EIP stöder sina medlemmar i deras utveckling av ansvariga, inkluderande och transparenta offentliga institutioner som kan leverera effektiva policys och program för fattigdomsbekämpning och hållbar utveckling.
EIP startades 2012 som ett svar på internationella åtaganden om behovet av stärkt effektivitet hos offentliga institutioner, och har sedan dess utvecklats till en mekanism för innovation och kollegialt utbyte mellan myndigheter. OECD är värd och sekretariat för plattformen, men till skillnad från andra P2P mekanismer inom ramen för OECD riktar sig EIP bortom organisationens egna medlemsstater, och har idag mer än 60 medlemmar. Dessa innefattar både givar- och partnerländer, utvecklingsbanker, civilsamhällesorganisationer och FN organ.
EIPs övergripande mål är att bidra till uppfyllandet av Agenda 2030, i synnerhet Mål 16 och biståndseffektivitetsagendan, genom att fungera som en global kunskapsnav för "peer-to-peer" lärande, och en plattform för att facilitera utvecklingen av alternativa och innovativa metoder för reform och utveckling av den offentliga sektorn.

Insatsen ämnar finansiera genomförandet av EIP:s nya strategiska fokus och arbetsplan. Båda är ett resultat av omfattande omprioriteringar som ägt rum på EIP de senaste åren. Med stöd från bl.a. Sida har plattformen genomgått en s.k. revisioning process, då dess roll och mervärde i det förändrade utvecklingssammanhanget omvärderades.
Då intresset för peer-to-peer metoder, institutionell reform och utvecklingseffektivitet har ökat kraftigt sedan EIP:s grundande i 2012, har man definierat två nya strategiska fokusområden: (1) att agera som en global kunskapsbank och företrädare för Peer-to-peer (P2P) metoder, och (2) att tillhandahålla en plattform för att underlätta inkubation och lärande av innovativa strategier för reform och institutionell utveckling av offentlig sektor.
Insatsens mål är operationaliserandet av detta nya fokus. Detta förväntas resultera i att etablera EIP som ett globalt nav för innovativa metoder, att utveckla evidens för P2P lärande, och att stödja andra P2P nätverk.
Sekretariatet kommer att använda Sidas kärnstöd för att: 1. Upprätthålla information över P2P-allianser och relevanta kunskapsnav i syfte att identifiera och starta nya partnerskap. 2. Sammanställa evidens för effektiviteten av olika P2P-metoder och innovativa verktyg som stödjer institutionella utveckling i den offentliga sektorn. 3. Kommunicera och förespråka kunskap och lärande från P2P-partnerskap och innovativa metoder. 4. Stöda EIP-medlemmar att stärka sina strategier för peer-to-peer lärande och innovativa metoder som effektiva verktyg för att bidra till institutionell utveckling på nationell, regional eller internationell nivå. 5. Organisera årliga möten för medlemmar för gemensamt lärande och kunskapsutbyte samt för att granska och/eller förnya EIP:s mål och befintliga styrning.
EIPs arbete bedöms ha potential att bidra till att bygga upp effektiva, transparenta och inkluderande institution med ansvarsutkrävande på all nivåer i partnerländer, något som är centralt för Agenda 2030:s mål 16.

sector.narrative: Public sector policy and administrative management

description.narrative:
The overall objective and focus of the EIP was institution development, SDG 16.6, peertopeer learning and Monitoring EvaluationLearning (MEL) as a tool and EIP as the global knowledge hub and platform for learning and innovative approaches to public sector reform and institutional development.
Given the outlined tasks for the 20212022 programme, the EIP has achieved these overall results:
i) Maintain a register of P2P alliances, knowledge hubs and communities of practice with a view to identify and sustain prospective EIP and P2P partnerships.
The EIP maintained a register of different P2P alliances, knowledge hubs and communities of practice with a comprehensive website and the mailing list as means for the membership of the EIP to disseminate EIP material and communication. The EIP website also contained a specific web page for Tools and Approaches which composes a repository of innovative tools, methodologies and practices on P2P learning. In terms of partnerships, the first year of the programme was productive with several learning events in terms of bilateral and partner engagements. A highlight of this partner engagement was that EIP managed to convene through the 2021 Annual Meeting external speakers and facilitator of a P2P alliance on anti-corruption authorities between Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda and Zambia together with other engaged members to reflect on EIP partner experiences. The quality of partnerships improved in 2022 through the engagement with the Maarifa Centre and UCLG. ii/iii. Work with EIP members to build evidence on the merits of varying P2P approaches (and identify, establish and update a repository of innovative tools, methodologies and practices), and conduct a number of interactive learning events on effective P2P ways of working.
During the two year period, but mostly in 2021, the EIP managed to produce and publish a series of knowledge products as evidence for learning and methods of P2P. Most prominently is the Lessons Harvesting: Learning from P2P Engagements Discussion Paper for a Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Framework, which highlights seven key features of good practice approaches to monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL) in P2P learning and how these approaches can be used to deliver better results for institutional development. Building on these insights that aimed to generate evidence and insights on good practices in P2P learning, the EIP launched a Learning Event series, comprising three virtual events held between December 2020 and May 2021. The events reflected on key attributes of effective P2P partnerships, and considered the role of MEL in tracking and supporting these approaches. The events facilitated reflection and exchange among more than 120 established practitioners in OECD and non-OECD countries, providing opportunities for participants to learn from existing P2P partnerships and to share their own experiences of enabling change through P2P and alternative approaches to reform.
These learning events resulted in richer exchanges among P2P practitioners and provided important inputs to three learning notes that were prepared and published in December 2021. These Learning Notes highlighted several of the key attributes of effective partnerships for development including: (i) the importance of building trust and mutuality, (ii) the function of learning through interconnected systems and (iii) the need to adapt P2P approaches to unleash local capabilities. These notes were designed to be used as reference tools by EIP members and partners to guide and enhance their approach to P2P partnerships. In addition to highlighting key insights in relation to these attributes, the learning notes also proposed key questions for P2P practitioners to explore. The notes are considered organic resources to be revised and updated as new insights emerge, which had been disseminated through the EIPs website, social media (Twitter), and through a dedicated session at the Annual Meeting and internally at the OECDs Development Cooperation Directorate All Staff meeting.
iv) Develop, test and publish a MEL framework for P2P approaches to institutional development with the aim of ensuring uptake by partner institutions and EIP members alike.
The work to develop, test and publish a monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL) framework made good progress during this reporting period. A Roadmap was created in September 2021 outlining the process for implementation of this work stream by the Secretariat to co-create, adapt and pilot test tools in existing member and partnerled P2P partnerships. The roadmap sets out the purpose and principles for engagement, dividing the process into five distinct phases including (i) engaging MEL pilot partners in co-creation, (ii) problem identification and self-assessment, (iii) tools development, (iv) piloting and adjusting tools and (v) feedback and documentation of lessons.
To pilot test and cocreate MEL tools and approaches with the EIP Secretariat, the United Cities and Local Governments (UCLG) and the Maarifa Centre in Kenya were selected for the engagement roadmaps in March 2022 after a broaden application process that involved proposals, apart from the two selected, also from the GIZ Anti Corruption Authorities (ACAs) project and UK Revenue and Customs department. This engagement roadmaps identify the parameters for engagement:
- The guiding criteria for selection include the type of P2P arrangement at hand, ensuring the presence of different actors and sectors, having the necessary scope and time for involving national/local actors in the localisation of tools and approaches (also to secure their ownership in the process), have a degree of mutuality and ideally select P2P arrangements at the early stage of formation to introduce and codesign MEL approaches from the outset. - UCLG and the Secretariat have agreed to review the ways in which peer learning has been captured and utilised in their Mediterranean City-to-City Migration (MC2CM) project. The principal tool adopted based on outcome harvesting was intended to result in a joint publication to be showcased at the UCLG World Congress in October 2022. - The Maarifa Centre is a knowledge sharing and learning platform supporting the Kenyan Council of Governors, which is a nonpartisan organisation comprising the Governors of the 47 Kenyan Counties supporting decentralization.
The engagement and partnership of the EIP with the two UCLG and Maarifa Centre to cocreate, adapt and pilottest a set of monitoring, evaluation and learning tools to better track and deliver results through P2P partnership approaches gave some observations: - From the engagement with the UCLG: The EIP concluded a roadmap with UCLG whose principle objective was to review the role and contribution of P2P learning in UCLGs Mediterranean CitytoCity Migration (MC2CM) programme. This was to identifying what worked and what did not work, in terms of strategies for P2P learning, and identifying specific MEL approaches that could better deliver results, either as part of the MC2CM programme going forward or in the context of future UCLG programming. The MC2CM project connects 22 cities to improve and facilitate urban migration governance. Led by the United Nations Human Settlements Program (UNHabitat), the International Centre for Migration Policy Development (ICMPD) and UCLG, it addresses the critical theme of migration governance across the Mediterranean. The MC2CM has organized 16 peer learning events focusing on interactive learning among using innovative and interactive tools such as field visits or games. Reviewing the leverage of the Mediterranean City-to-City Migration Project through a report published in May 2023, positive effects of P2P learning in the MC2CM project. reflected how it (i) better equipped cities to engage in migration governance (ii) improved cities resilience against shocks (3) facilitated the establishment of a platform for new contacts across cities (4) allowed city level actions funded by MC2CM or inspired by other cities and (5) politically empowered participating cities. - From the engagement with the Maarifa Centre: During 2022, the EIP trained Council of Governors (CoG) sectoral committees on P2P learning using How-to-guide on P2P learning which was tailored to the Kenyan context of operation and included several sections on monitoring, evaluation and learning for P2P. This also equipped CoG staff with innovative knowledge and skills that they can disseminate to 47 Counties to apply as methodology to local solutions for both institutional and service delivery challenges. In December 2022, the EIP and Maarifa Centre organized a workshop on Investing in Inter-County Peer Learning as a Strategy for Institutional Reform to highlight showcases for counties to learn from similar reforms regarding digitalisation of community health services and youth empowerment. This workshop involved 13 counties in Kenya to showcase, learn from experiences and inspiration for inter-county peer learning, as well as participated in interactive problem solving exercises based on the problem solving iterative adaptation methodology. As a way forward, Counties developed action plans to entrench P2P learning for institutional reform.
The EIP partnership with the UCLG and Maarifa Centre in Kenya indicated that results from the partnership in terms of how-to-guide on P2P learning and MEL methodology to track outcomes of P2P learning for institutional development will be likely be used in their future engagement with other partners, beyond the engagement with the EIP.
v) Facilitate outreach and engagement to communicate knowledge and learning from P2P partnerships and hold annual meetings for members on learning and knowledge sharing. - The EIPs outreach and engagement increased during the reporting period with the Secretariat engaged varying partners championing P2P learning to explore opportunities for closer collaboration, coordination and improved uptake of EIPs tools and approaches. The EIP has also taken opportunities to showcase the EIP's work with the Practitioners Network for European Development Cooperation and in the context of the OECDDACs Peer Reviews, including Portugal and the US. To increase outreach activities in line with the guidance of the Advisory Group and EIP joint CoChairs, the EIP developed an Outreach and Sector Engagement Strategy to guide outreach activities. The purpose of this strategy is to expand the knowledge, learning and experience of effective ways of P2P working across EIP members and P2P communities, and create opportunities for collaboration and support among prospective partners. It also includes increasing the diversity of EIP members and partners as well as better adapting and tailoring engagement, outreach and dissemination to the needs, problems and types of partnerships within and beyond the membership. Adopted in November 2021, the strategy has not been fully implemented since the 2022 was focused on preparing the transition for the EIP to a new organisational host. - Annual Meeting was held only in 2021 since 2022 was focused on preparation for EIP transition and finding a new organisational host. The Secretariat continued to support EIP members to promote and strengthen their approaches towards P2P and alternative approaches on a demand basis. For example, the EIP was engaged with Senegal working on labour law reform where the partner country requested to participate in the co-creation and piloting of MEL tools to track results and impacts in P2P partnerships. the EIP also promoted the importance of MEL for tracking and measuring the impact of P2P learning through presentations at the UCLG Learning Forum Session on the 31st May 2022.
In sum, during Sida's contribution period of 01.01.2021 31.03.2023, the EIP has contributed its knowledge and learning methodology on measuring and tracking the impacts of P2P learning through the development and production of a series of learning notes based on a series of public webinars held between December 2020 and May 2021, developed an Outreach and Sector Engagement Strategy and finalised an updated Workplan for 20212022, developed a roadmap to pilot test MEL tools and approaches for P2P learning, convened partners exchange in 2021 and completed its commitments with the United Cities and Local Governments (UCLG) and the Maarifa Centre (knowledge and learning hub of the Council of Governors in Kenya) to co-create, adapt and pilot test a set of monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL) tools. These partnerships culminated in the publication of a Howto guide on P2P learning, P2P learning case studies on the digitisation of community health care and youth innovation and empowerment centres between Kenyan Counties and a joint report with UCLG on Leveraging the potential of peer learning for local governments: A review of the Mediterranean CitytoCity Migration Project.
Most of the programme targeted interventions were mainly conducted during 2021 and workplans outlined by its 20212022 Strategy could partly be executed during 2021 only due to the most part of 2022 was preparation for the EIP to transit to a host organisation.
